> VERDICT: OK with notes. Review-2 P1-1 is closed and the grant fix is sound. Review-3 T1, T2 and T4 are still owed and still gate the merge. D1 has grown (below).
> 
> 5a, review-2 P1-1 CLOSED.
> - in_callback() is HANDLING_IRQ, set only when irq::interrupt_owner(irq) is Some, as the kernel starts a callback, and cleared only in finish_isr. Both in_irq arguments use it.
> - A source with no handler is masked and records no callback. PREVIOUS_PAIR is set only beside HANDLING_IRQ, so finish_isr's expect is now consistent.
> - ReturnToParent returns UnhandledSyscall. Callers: I grep'd the tree excluding target and vendor, and the only one is the new attack test; set_isr_return_pair is gone.
> - P3: the attack case bites only at its first check. A future regression that re-keys in_callback on something else user-settable would not be caught by the deadline and steward checks, because nothing reaches them pre-fix. Consider a second child that skips ReturnToParent and tries the next plausible trigger (e.g. a RETURN_FROM_ISR jump with no callback running), so the later checks are exercised on their own.
> - P3 hardening: finish_isr ends a callback for any process that faults at RETURN_FROM_ISR while HANDLING_IRQ is set. If any legacy call allowed in a callback (TrySendMessage non-blocking, ReturnScalar/ReturnMemory) can direct-switch to another process, that process could end someone else's callback. Check in finish_isr that current is the handler owner on IRQ_TID, and otherwise treat it as a plain fault.
> 
> 5b CLOSED.
> - Grants: grant_for honours a Grnt tag only when process::object_of(pid) is None, i.e. loader programs. I checked that this can't be undone. Every process-object free path (settle_notice, receive of the notice, budgets_dying, endpoint_dying, free_object) either runs after the process is dead or asserts !alive (free_object), so a live created process always has its object and never gains a grant. random_free_pid also skips PIDs still named by an object.
> - Other PID-keyed authority, none inherited:
>   - legacy IRQ claims are released at terminate (release_interrupts_for_pid, services.rs:293);
>   - legacy servers and connections by release_servers_of and tombstones;
>   - frames by release_all_memory_for_process;
>   - the sched cursor (pid, tid) is only an ordering hint;
>   - SWITCHTO_CALLER and PREVIOUS_PAIR hold kmain, or a live pair during a callback.
>   Legacy ConnectForProcess(pid, sid) takes an arbitrary PID but is pre-existing and not grant authority.
> - The other 5b items: every finish_isr now rearms; all-together has timer coverage again (a sleeper) and passes at smp 1 and 2; expiry walks are billed per found item, with at most one unpaid walk per entry; SPP is read once, at entry.
> 
> 5c CLOSED on review-1 P2-1..4 and the P3s.
> - redoubt_stride::Cpu is the kernel's wiring (accrue, bill, settle, change_weight, switch with MIN_CHARGE, reconcile, pick, create, destroy), and the differential drives that same Cpu. Deschedule now passes still_runnable, so the counters match the model exactly.
> - MIN_CHARGE plus R12NoMinimumCharge (caught by sched_contracts).
> - The saturating lift and weight asserts, and the insert/reconcile loop guards.
> - Sensitivity numbers:
>   - (k) 3000/3000 against R12LiftCountsEntryWait;
>   - (b) 2959/3000 against PreemptOnWake;
>   - (d) 1376/3000 against R12DropRemainder. That is enough: mutation detection needs any reliable catch, and a 46% per-seed rate is effectively certain within the family's cap. The exact fold check in (l) also catches it.
> - The per-step bottom-up carve return matches plan s1, and the differential found the divergence (seed 75), which is the tool working. But see D1.
> 
> STILL OWED (review-3; unchanged in these commits, confirmed by running them):
> - T1: exit-churn is unchanged. Each churn child and worker still sends its report before exiting, so the exit path is untested. Victim 494/494/497.
> - T2: budget-churn variants 0-3 are still insensitive (attacker subtree 10/22/0/10 of 1000; victim 948/494/976/946). The new variant (e) is sensitive to the entry-persistence bug, but with thin margins: committed 535 vs a mutant 555 against a bound of 550, i.e. 15 and 5 units. It is deterministic under icount but fragile to any kernel timing change. Widen the gap, e.g. more back-to-back creates per slice, or assert the parent pass delta through the sched-trace oracle.
> - T4: nothing at boot shows a timeout never preempts.
> 
> D1 (design; for the orchestrator's ruling), now worse. Moving the top's carve return from mark time to its own lift step (5c, to match plan s1) means a parent's budget_destroy of a child now pays R10's ~21 ms at the parent's carved-down free weight. The destroy syscall's time accrues to the parent's pending until the top's lift settles it at the old weight. With the plan's shell (carving 99 of 100), each command's teardown costs the parent about 100 x 21 ms of wait. Together with the earlier findings (carved-down runtime charged at the kept weight; lift inflation by limit/free), a (k)-shaped honest shell is starved, and the case sits at weight 50 because of it (victim 535, shell subtree 258). The options stay as in review-3 D1; add (c): settle and return the top's carve at mark time as before, and mirror that in the model and plan s1 (the per-step order was an arbitrary plan choice, and the mark-time order charges the destruction at the restored weight). My recommendation is (c) plus (b).

### Orchestrator · Instruction

Event: `f5309df4ff61761132655574b16f483d` · 2026-09-24T22:39:41Z

> The red team passed review 4 (5a, 5b, 5c) as OK with notes: P1-1 closed, the PID-reuse grant fix sound, review 1 closed. Rulings and remaining items:
> D1, now a ruling (the red team shows it got worse with the per-step carve return): R10 destruction work (~21 ms) is billed to the parent at its CARVED-DOWN weight. Example: init in root with 1000 free weight destroys a big user subtree, gains a huge lead, and is starved. Fix: return the TOP's carve at mark time, before any destruction work is billed, so the destruction is charged at the parent's restored weight. That's what OWNER DECISION 6's intent and commit 5's message said. Keep the per-step bottom-up return for inner nodes if the differential needs it, but the top's weight must be back before billing. Change the model, redoubt-stride and the kernel together so the differential still agrees, and add a case: a small-free-weight parent destroying a large-weight child gets no lead beyond one slice's worth for the destruction. Rescaling the lead on every weight increase stays a follow-up (QA K5-carve-lead-rescale); don't do it now.
> Still owed, and they gate merge: T1 (exit-churn must end the spin directly by exit, fault or thread_exit), T2 (budget-churn variants 0-3 are insensitive, and the new shell variant's margins are thin: 535 vs 555 against 550; widen them or use the sched-trace oracle), T4 (a boot check that a timeout doesn't preempt).
> P3s: make callback-state-attack check every stage, not just the first; finish_isr must verify the caller is the callback's owner.
> Report at your next checkpoint.
